structure: Part 1, version mount, layout and journey control, read at commit c2078fb (the checkout's HEAD). Read in full: app/lib/version-mount.js (365 lines: shared session keys, the 35 journey path prefixes, shared paths, path prefixing for redirects and render data, the version session nest, the view-override rule, router copying), app/lib/design-release-2.1-version.js (42 lines: base path, session key, version flag, reserved other base /testing, the render locals), app/config.json, app/filters.js and app/data/session-data-defaults.js (both empty), app/utils/notification-reference.js (the testing-format GB.<year>.<sequence> - <type> helpers), layouts/main.html (header and the four service-navigation branches), layouts/journey.html (two-thirds column and the cancel-amend dialog include), index.html (the service index: two design cards and three testing cards), partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html (template-review, amend, template-create and default modes), both notification-status partials and the notification-reference macro, and app/routes.js lines 1-40 (requires only), 57-96 (constants, the notification references, isDesignRelease21SessionData), 308-509 (version flags, references, dashboard reference mapping, session reset, the reason-for-import seed), 548-607 (from-hub, from-review, template-review return, back links), 1711-1825 (step order, next path, amend test, form actions, save and section redirects), 8202-8263 (design release 2 test, version base path, address book href, dashboard back link), 13494-13497 (GET /index), 15140-15142 (sign-in redirect) and 15332-15341 (mount order). Helper bodies outside these ranges (gross weight, identifiers, additional details, transit, template create, hub complete, reference generator, the /prototype/reason-for-import and /create-notification handlers) were looked up only to state the step conditions; their pages are other parts'. The cancel-amend dialog's own content is part 12's (it reads partials/design-release-2.1/cancel-amend-modal.html), so this part claims only when the layout includes it. Covered: the /design-release-2.1 mount, session nest, prefixing and view fallback; the version flags and which apply to DR2.1; the service navigation, header and service index; the journey form actions and status bar; the step order and next-page rules; the reference format and dashboard mapping; session reset; back-link and return rules; sign-in redirect and GET /index.

claims.statement: Design release 2.1 is served under the base path /design-release-2.1.

Every route of the root router is copied under /design-release-2.1 (each method of each route, with the same handlers), so DR2.1 has the same pages and handlers as the root journey rather than its own route table.
Only route layers are copied into the version router: router-level middleware and the catch-all _all method are not copied.
claims.note: mechanism: copies the root router's route table into the version router.

claims.statement: The versions are mounted in the order Testing 4, Testing 3, Testing and then Design release 2.1; the longer /testing paths go before /testing so they are not taken as /testing paths. No separate design release 2 version is mounted.
claims.quote:
// Mount the longer /testing* paths before /testing so Express does not treat them as that route
mountTesting4Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTesting3Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTestingVersion(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountDesignRelease21Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)

claims.statement: Under /design-release-2.1 the session data a page sees is a separate nest stored under the session key _designRelease21, so DR2.1 notifications, drafts and answers are kept apart from the root journey and the other versions.
Inside the DR2.1 session nest the flag _isDesignRelease21Version is set to true on every request, which handlers use to tell they are running as DR2.1.

Two session keys are shared across all versions rather than kept in the DR2.1 nest: the addresses added to the address book (addressBookAddedAddresses) and the submitted notifications (submittedNotifications). Reading or writing them in DR2.1 reads or writes the shared value.

When a DR2.1 request carries a form or query field (not starting with an underscore, not the session key and not a shared key) whose name also exists in the shared session outside the DR2.1 nest, the nest takes the outer session's value for that key before the handler runs.
claims.note: mechanism: copies outer session values into the version nest. The posted value itself is applied later by the prototype kit. Recorded as observed, not interpreted further.

claims.statement: Before a DR2.1 response redirects or ends, the session is restored so the DR2.1 nest is saved back under _designRelease21 in the full session.
claims.note: mechanism: saves the version session nest.

claims.statement: Every DR2.1 page is given the requested URL, query string included, as currentPath.

In DR2.1, a redirect to a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1 (for example a redirect to /notification-hub goes to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub), and a redirect to / goes to /design-release-2.1.

A link or redirect to / with a query string (/?...) becomes /design-release-2.1?... in DR2.1, and a journey path keeps its query string and fragment after the prefix; whether a path is a journey path is decided on the path without its query string or fragment.

In DR2.1, every string in the data passed to a page render that is a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so links, form actions and back links built by handlers stay inside the version.
claims.note: mechanism: rewrites every string in a page's render data, nested objects and arrays and the data object included.

claims.statement: The journey path prefixes that are kept inside the version are: /create-notification, /notification-type, /origin-of-the-import, /what-are-you-importing, /reason-for-import, /consignment-details, /consignment-gross-weight, /animal-identification-details, /additional-animal-details, /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /upload-documents, /roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /contact-address-for-consignment, /review-notification, /declaration, /notification-submitted, /notification-hub, /notifications, /dashboard, /live-animals, /germinal-products, /templates, /actions, /changes, /inspection and /prototype/reason-for-import (each path itself or anything below it).
Paths that are not journey paths are left unprefixed: external or protocol-relative links, links not starting with /, fragment links starting with #, and any path not in the journey prefix list.

The address book (/address-book and anything below it), static assets (/public/, /plugin-assets/), the prototype kit management pages (/manage-prototype) and the service index (/index) are shared paths that are never prefixed with the version base path.
claims.quote:
return urlPath === '/address-book' ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/address-book/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/public/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/plugin-assets/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/manage-prototype') ||
    urlPath === '/index'

claims.statement: A path that already starts with /design-release-2.1 or /testing is never prefixed again, so DR2.1 links into the Round 1 testing version are left as they are.
claims.note: /testing3 and /testing4 are not reserved bases, but they are not journey prefixes either, so they are left unprefixed by the general rule.

claims.statement: When DR2.1 renders a page, it uses the page's override in app/views/design-release-2.1/ when one exists (as .html, .njk or a folder index.html), and otherwise falls back to the root view of the same name. Layouts, partials and govuk or moj templates are never swapped this way.

DR2.1 pages are also treated as design release 2 pages: every DR2.1 render has isDesignRelease2Version and isDesignRelease21Version set, and the session check for design release 2 is true for DR2.1 sessions, so design release 2 behaviour applies under /design-release-2.1 unless a DR2.1 branch overrides it.
Every DR2.1 page has journeyBasePath set to /design-release-2.1, which partials use to build version-local links.
The handler test for design release 2.1 is the _isDesignRelease21Version flag; the routes.js comment says Design release 2.1, Testing 3 and Testing 4 all set it.
claims.quote: // Those are the three versions that set the Design release 2.1 flag.

claims.statement: The November 2026 journey updates (identification fields by commodity, removable addresses and transporter, blank-friendly templates, dashboard dates and Amend examples, address book uses) apply under /design-release-2.1, because hasJourneyUpdates is true whenever the Design release 2.1 flag is set.
Branches guarded by isRound2TestingSessionData (Testing 3 or Testing 4) do not apply under /design-release-2.1, because DR2.1 sets neither testing flag.
claims.note: Inferred: the DR2.1 mount sets only _isDesignRelease21Version, never _isTesting3Version or _isTesting4Version.

claims.statement: Branches guarded by isDesignRelease21OnlySessionData apply under /design-release-2.1: it is true when the Design release 2.1 flag is set and neither the Testing 2 flag nor a Round 2 testing flag is.
Under /design-release-2.1 the contact address for consignment question is left out: omitsContactAddressQuestion is true for DR2.1 (as it is for Testing 3 and 4).
Under /design-release-2.1 documents are not worded as "Health certificate": that wording is used only by the Round 2 prototypes (Testing 3 and 4).
claims.quote: // Round 2 prototypes use "Health certificate" document wording.
claims.note: Inferred from usesHealthCertificateWording returning isRound2TestingSessionData, which is false for DR2.1. The documents pages' own wording is another part's.

claims.statement: Signing in (POST /intro/sign-in) takes the user to the DR2.1 dashboard at /design-release-2.1.
The fixed design-release notification reference is GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P; the testing version uses GB.2026.7963913 - CHEDA instead.
A design-release notification reference has the form GBN-, two letters, a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen and then letters or digits (matched case-insensitively), such as GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P.

When a notification has no reference, or its reference is not in the design-release format, a new reference GBN-AG-26- followed by six random upper-case letters or digits is generated, avoiding the fixed reference and every reference already used on the dashboard, in drafts and in submitted notifications.
claims.note: The generator's body sits in another part's range; it builds `GBN-AG-26-${code}` from a six-character random code and skips any reference in the existing set.

claims.statement: Under /design-release-2.1 the notification reference is always in the GBN design-release format: the testing-format (GB.<year>.<sequence> - <type>) references are used only by the Round 1 testing version and by Testing 3 and 4.
claims.note: Inferred: DR2.1 sets neither _isTestingVersion nor a Round 2 testing flag, so it reaches only the design-release branch.

claims.statement: The notification reference utility formats testing-format references as GB.<year>.<sequence> - <type>, defaulting to GB.2026.7963913 - CHEDA; under DR2.1 none of its output is shown, because routes.js uses it only to build Testing 3 and 4 dashboard references.
claims.note: Inferred: routes.js is the only file that requires the utility, and it imports only formatNotificationReference and the two defaults, used in toTesting3DashboardReference. The utility's other helpers (submitted-reference test, legacy-reference test, normalising, ensureDraftNotificationReference and a random submitted sequence from 7000000) are not called in scope.

claims.statement: Seed dashboard notifications whose reference is in the testing format are shown with a design-release reference: the first notification, and any with sequence 7963913, show GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P; others show GBN-AG-26- followed by a six-character code derived from their sequence number.
A dashboard notification whose reference is already in the design-release format keeps that reference unchanged under DR2.1.

Starting a new notification journey clears every answer in the version's session, but keeps the added address book addresses, draft notifications, deleted notification references, submitted notifications, saved templates and deleted template ids (each only when not empty), along with the Testing, Design release 2.1, Testing 2, Testing 3 and Testing 4 session nests.

The journey session is reset when the user starts a notification at /create-notification, which also clears the creating-a-template flag; other entry points reset it too (called at app/routes.js 6835, 6860, 9819, 9842, 9876, 10407, 10451, 10471, 13295, 13349 and 13918).
claims.note: The other call sites belong to other parts' pages (templates, copy, amend, dashboard); they are listed so the reconciler can find them.

claims.statement: The prototype shortcut /prototype/reason-for-import seeds a notification (origin France, no region of origin, commodity Cattle 0102, species cattle-bison-bison with 5 animals, certification purpose Slaughter, unweaned animals No, a design-release reference) and goes straight to the reason for import page.
claims.note: A designer shortcut, not a user-facing page; /prototype/reason-for-import is a DR2.1 journey prefix so it stays inside the version.

claims.statement: Germinal products have three temperature options, Ambient, Chilled and Frozen, and their quantity is labelled "Quantity (unit/pieces)".
claims.note: Constants in this part's lines; the pages that use them are other parts'.

claims.statement: A page is treated as reached from the notification overview (hub) when its query or form carries from=hub.
A page is treated as reached from the check-your-answers review page when its query or form carries from=review.
A page is treated as reached from a template review when its query or form carries from=template-review, or the session is marked as editing a template from its review.

The return path to a template review is /templates/<template id> (the template being edited, or the session's template), or /templates when there is no template id; in DR2.1 this becomes /design-release-2.1/templates/<id>.

Saving a page while editing a template from its review saves the template, sets the success message "<template title> has been updated." (using the template name, or "Template" when it has neither title nor name), clears the template editing state, ends template creation and returns to that template's review page.

A journey page's back link goes to the template review when the page was reached from a template review, to the notification overview (/notification-hub) when reached from the hub, and otherwise to the previous page in the journey.

A page reached from the check-your-answers review page does not get a back link to the review: the back-link rule only special-cases template review and hub, so from=review pages fall back to the previous journey page.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of an isFromReview branch in getJourneyBackLink; individual pages may override their own back link.

claims.statement: The journey step order starts with origin of the import, what are you importing, reason for import and consignment details, in that order.
The consignment gross weight step follows consignment details only when the notification has germinal products only.
The animal identification details step comes after consignment details and any gross weight step, only when at least one selected species has identifier fields.
The additional animal details step comes next only when that page would ask the certification purpose question or the unweaned animals question.
Arrival details is always a step, after the animal steps.
The transit countries step follows arrival details only when the means of transport is Rail or Road.
Means of transport values are normalised before the transit check: airplane and air mean Air; railway and rail mean Rail; road vehicle and road mean Road; vessel and sea mean Sea.
claims.quote:
airplane: 'Air',
  air: 'Air',
  railway: 'Rail',
  rail: 'Rail',
  'road vehicle': 'Road',
  road: 'Road',
  vessel: 'Sea',
  sea: 'Sea'

claims.statement: Transporter is always a step, after arrival details and any transit countries.
In DR2.1, the upload documents step is skipped when the user is creating a template; otherwise it follows transporter.
Roles and addresses is always a step, after documents (or after transporter when creating a template).
The contact address for consignment step follows roles and addresses only when the version asks the contact address question, so under /design-release-2.1 it is not a step.
Review notification is always a step, after roles and addresses (and contact address where a version asks it).
In DR2.1, the declaration step after review is skipped when the user is creating a template; otherwise declaration is the last step.

Under /design-release-2.1 the full linear order is: origin of the import, what are you importing, reason for import, consignment details, gross weight (germinal products only), animal identification details (when needed), additional animal details (when needed), arrival details, transit countries (Rail or Road only), transporter, upload documents (not for templates), roles and addresses, review notification, declaration (not for templates).
claims.note: Inferred by applying the DR2.1 flags (contact address omitted) to getJourneySteps.

claims.statement: The step order has no step for CPH number, permanent address, place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination; those pages are reached from within roles and addresses or the hub, not as linear steps.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing getJourneySteps with JOURNEY_PATH_PREFIXES (app/lib/version-mount.js:11-47), which lists those paths. How they are reached is other parts' business.

claims.statement: The next page after a step is the following step in the order; after the last step, or from a page that is not a step, the next page is the notification overview (/notification-hub) unless the caller gives another fallback.
The current page is matched against the step order without its query string.
After roles and addresses, the next page is the notification overview instead of contact address for consignment when every notification hub section is already complete.
claims.note: Under DR2.1 the step after roles and addresses is review notification (contact address is omitted), so this sends a complete notification to the overview instead of the review.

claims.statement: A notification is being amended when its status is exactly Amend.
Journey forms send the button pressed as the action field; hub and review are soft-save actions (save and leave the linear flow), and continue moves on.

When a journey page is saved, the notification is persisted as a draft; then the action review goes to the review page (/review-notification), the action hub goes to the notification overview (/notification-hub), and any other action goes to the next page.
When a journey page is saved while editing a template from its review, the save returns to the template review and does not persist a draft notification.

When a section page continues, it returns to the template review if reached from one, to the notification overview if reached from the hub, to the review page if reached from review, and otherwise to the next page in the journey; the template review takes precedence over hub, and hub over review.

By default a DR2.1 journey page shows a primary "Save and continue" button (action continue), a secondary "Save and return to overview" button (action hub) and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification overview (/design-release-2.1/notification-hub).
A page may change the default actions: rename any of the three, hide the save and return to overview button, hide the cancel link, or point the cancel link elsewhere.
claims.quote:
{% set showHub = true if options.showHub is not defined else options.showHub %}
{% set showCancel = true if options.showCancel is not defined else options.showCancel %}

claims.statement: While creating a template (and not editing one from its review), a journey page's secondary button reads "Save and return to template" and its cancel link reads "Cancel and return to template" and goes to the Review your template page (/design-release-2.1/review-notification), ignoring any cancel link the page sets.

When a notification is being amended, a journey page shows a primary "Save and return" button (action review, going to the review page), a secondary "Save and continue" button (action continue) and a link-styled "Save and return to overview" button (action hub); there is no cancel link.

When the user is editing a template from its review, a journey page shows only a primary "Save and return" button (action continue, which returns to the template review) and a "Cancel" link to the template's page; this mode takes precedence over amend.

The template review Cancel link is built in the page as /templates/<template id> and is not prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so in DR2.1 it points at the root templates path rather than the version's.
claims.note: Inferred: version prefixing applies to redirects and render data, not to hrefs built inside a template. Possibly a prototype defect; the cancel href for the default mode uses journeyBasePath and is prefixed.

claims.note: The testing flags are checked before the DR2.1 flag, so a testing version that also sets the DR2.1 flag gets its own base path.

claims.statement: The dashboard is the DR2.1 home: the version base path /design-release-2.1 is the Dashboard navigation target and the dashboard back-link target.
claims.note: What GET / renders under DR2.1 is the dashboard part's to claim; this records only that the base path is used as the dashboard link.

claims.statement: The prototype defines no custom Nunjucks filters and no default session data.
